name: Standing orders funded by a steady salary mid-period: funded inflows credited to after payments and low point (G359, G360)

expected.notes: Calendar-month pay (payday Sun 1 Nov), today Mon 19 Oct 2026, so days to payday is 13 and the window is strictly the 13 days before it (days 0 to 12). The salary (3,000, two sightings 22 Aug and 22 Sep, 31 days apart, equal, monthly rhythm, largest credit on Barclays, due before payday) is a steady salary and is credited to Barclays on Thu 22 Oct (day 3), together with two standing orders from Barclays that it funds: 900 to HSBC and 500 to NatWest, also day 3. Bills: council tax 150 (Barclays, Tue 20 Oct, day 1), HSBC mortgage 800 (Wed 28 Oct, day 9), NatWest water 30 (Thu 29 Oct, day 10). Left to spend: pooled 350 + 60 + 40 = 450; the own-account standing orders remove neither leg; day 1: 450 - 150 = 300; day 3: + 3,000 salary = 3,300; day 9: - 800 = 2,500; day 10: - 30 = 2,470. The lowest point is the opening-side 300, so Left to spend 300. Barclays walk (credits before debits on a shared day): 350 - 150 = 200 (day 1); day 3: + 3,000 = 3,200, - 900 = 2,300, - 500 = 1,800. After payments 1,800, low point 200. G360 funded-inflow rule (services/inflow_credit.py): an inbound own-account transfer counts only if its source is covered that day. Barclays after everything up to day 3 is 1,800 >= 0, so both standing orders are funded and credited to their destinations; that holds only because the steady salary is credited (without it Barclays would sit at -1,200 on day 3 and neither would be). HSBC: 60, day 3 + 900 = 960, day 9 mortgage - 800 = 160. After payments 160; low point is the lowest running balance, 60 (the opening balance; the inflow lifts it, so the mortgage never takes it below 60: without the credit it would read 60 - 800 = -740, the HSBC case). NatWest: 40, + 500 = 540, - 30 = 510; after payments 510, low point 40. Spend from is the smaller of after payments and low point: Barclays 200, HSBC 60, NatWest 40, all below the pool 300. Nobody is short: no cover move, at risk 0. The period is on day 19 (1 Oct is day 1), so there is no payday plan (companion.py:2558, days_into_period <= 3).
